gloss: to meet face-to-face; to see each other

definitions.gloss: to meet face-to-face; to see each other in person
definitions.explanation: Describes meeting someone in person, often implying a direct encounter rather than a planned meeting. Can carry a nuance of awkwardness or inevitability when the encounter is unwanted.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせる。
examples.english: I see my neighbor face-to-face every morning.

examples.japanese: ⟦けんかした→けんかする：01634_kenkasuru⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせる⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{気|き}まずい→気まずい：06536_kimazui⟧。
examples.english: It's awkward to see each other after a fight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{久|ひさ}しぶり→久しぶり：01711_hisashiburi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦{全員|ぜんいん}→全員：03310_zenin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせて、⟦にぎやか→にぎやか：00873_nigiyaka⟧な⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧になった。
examples.english: The whole family got together for the first time in a while, and it was a lively meal.

notes:
USAGE:
A common set phrase for meeting someone in person. Unlike ⟦{会|あ}う→会う：00482_au⟧, which simply means "to meet," {顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせる emphasizes the face-to-face aspect and can imply an unplanned or unavoidable encounter.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせる (to see each other every day)
- {顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせるたび⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (every time we meet)
- {顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせにくい (hard to face someone)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{合|あ}わす: casual variant of the same expression
- ⟦{対面|たいめん}する→対面する：21377_taimen⟧: to meet face-to-face — more formal, typically for planned meetings
